claims.text: Thermal activation of the metastable solid solution triggers diffusion-limited nucleation and growth.
The thermally activated transformation produces discrete Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates disrupt the integrity of the passive oxide layer.
Disruption of the passive oxide layer reduces corrosion resistance.
Disruption of the passive oxide layer reduces high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The initial non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution state is produced by high-pressure/high-temperature processing.
During thermal aging, Mg atoms diffuse and nucleate intermetallic compounds.
The transformation proceeds by discrete intermetallic nucleation rather than by a continuous transformation.
Thermally aged samples will have a higher volume fraction of Mg-rich intermetallics than the as-processed state.
Thermally aged samples will have lower corrosion resistance than the as-processed state.
Thermally aged samples will have lower high-temperature oxidation resistance than the as-processed state.
The as-processed metastable state has intact passive layers.
The intact passive layers confer high corrosion resistance on the as-processed state.
The intact passive layers confer high oxidation resistance on the as-processed state.
Transformation and property degradation occur within the service-temperature range of 500–700°C.
Below 500°C, the metastable state remains largely intact.
In non-corrosive environments, the metastable state remains largely intact.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism select discrete nucleation and growth rather than continuous transformation, while the uncertainty field says the relative roles of discrete nucleation and spinodal-like decomposition remain speculative.

The transformation is described as thermally activated and diffusion-driven, but the boundary states that a non-corrosive environment should keep the metastable state intact. This makes corrosivity a condition for structural stability without explaining how it controls the proposed bulk thermal diffusion process.
